Ekman 60-faces task–EK-60F

description.value: The Ekman 60-Faces task (Ek-60F) assessed recognition of six basic emotions from 60 facial-expression photographs. Patients' performances were evaluated using Italian normative data, yielding a global score and single-emotion scores; it was administered to characterize socio-emotional processing deficits in probable bvFTD.

spans.text: The EK-60F is a well-known task of basic emotion recognition that consists of 60 b/w pictures from the Ekman and Friesen series of Picture of Facial Affect, which depict the faces of 10 actors, each displaying six basic emotions (i.e., happiness, sadness, anger, fear, surprise, disgust). Ek-60F patients’ performances were evaluated according to the Italian norms [ 38 ].

A second-level socio-emotional battery assessing the recognition of basic emotions from facial expression (Ekman 60-faces task–EK-60F) and the attribution of mental states to other individuals (Story-based Empathy Task–SET) was administered to each patient.

In order to evaluate the regional commonalities in the pattern of FDG-PET hypometabolism in the bvFTD patients performing at or below the 5  percentile in the tasks assessing processing of affective cues (i.e., Ek-60F global score and SET-EA sub-score) (n = 7;  Table 2 ), we computed a whole-brain group analysis (i.e., one-sample t-test) using the contrast images resulting from each first-order “single-subject” analysis.

description.value: The emotional-attribution subscale of the non-verbal Story-based Empathy Task (SET-EA) assessed attribution of emotional mental states to other individuals using original standardized cartoons. Adjusted scores based on Italian normative data were used to characterize socio-emotional processing deficits in probable bvFTD.

spans.text: The SET task is a non-verbal task, developed in our laboratory with original cartoons and standardized for the Italian population [ 39 ], which assessed attribution of mental states to other individuals requiring the recognition of their intentions (i.e., SET-IA) versus emotional states (i.e., SET-EA), as well as the ability to infer physical causal relationships (i.e., SET-CI) devoid of social components

description.value: The emotion recognition and attribution index (ERA) was a derived composite defined as (SET-EA × 10) + Ek-60F global score, combining facial emotion-recognition and emotional-attribution performance for correlation with FDG-PET metabolism.
